steps.text: Take Torsemide 20 mg once a day. Do not take furosemide anymore
Take Metoprolol succinate 75 mg once a day. Do not take the old metoprolol
Take Cephalexin 500 mg four times a day until it is gone (next 4 days)
Take Empagliflozin 10 mg once a day
Take Apixaban 5 mg twice a day, every day
Weigh yourself every day and write it down
Look at your right leg every day: redness, warmth and swelling should be shrinking
Get your kidney and electrolyte blood tests as ordered after the water pill change
See your primary care doctor (as arranged)
Put your right leg up when resting

medications.name: Torsemide
medications.why: Your new water pill. It replaces furosemide and takes extra fluid off. You will urinate more.

medications.name: Metoprolol succinate
medications.why: A long-acting version that keeps your heart rate steady. It replaces the old short-acting metoprolol.

medications.name: Cephalexin
medications.howOften: four times a day for 4 more days
medications.why: An antibiotic to finish treating the leg infection. Take every dose.

medications.name: Apixaban
medications.howOften: twice a day, as on your final medication list
medications.why: A blood thinner that prevents strokes from the irregular heartbeat. Never stop it without asking your doctor.

medications.name: Atorvastatin
medications.why: Lowers cholesterol to protect your heart.

medications.name: Home diabetes regimen
medications.howOften: as on your final medication list

medications.name: Furosemide
medications.why: Stopped. Torsemide replaces it. Do not take both water pills.

medications.name: Previous short-acting metoprolol regimen
medications.why: Stopped. The new once-a-day metoprolol succinate replaces it.

followUps.why: Check your heart rate, fluid and the new medicines
Check the leg infection and your blood tests

warnings.text: Severe or quickly worsening shortness of breath
A fast or irregular heartbeat that does not settle and makes you feel unwell
Swelling or weight going up quickly
The leg redness spreading past the marked line, or the pain getting much worse fast
Heavy bleeding while on the blood thinner
Dizziness or blood pressure changes, so we can check your fall risk
Any new drainage from the leg
